terms.household_wording: Name the operation, such as Turn on reading lamp
terms.first_use_explanation: An action asks Home Assistant to perform an operation or a sequence step.
terms.avoid_confusion: An action request is not an event, and acceptance does not prove the device completed it.

terms.household_wording: Use the device's actual control name
terms.first_use_explanation: An actor is an entity that can respond to a control request.
terms.avoid_confusion: This is a technical role, not a household member or a synonym for every entity.

terms.household_wording: App; explain formerly add-on when reading older instructions
terms.first_use_explanation: An app runs additional software alongside Home Assistant on Home Assistant OS.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not confuse an app with an integration, a dashboard card or the phone's Companion app.

terms.household_wording: Area, followed by the household's chosen name
terms.first_use_explanation: An area groups devices or entities by a room or other space.
terms.avoid_confusion: An area is not a geographic zone; targeting an area can affect several entities.

terms.household_wording: Automation; explain the trigger and intended action
terms.first_use_explanation: An automation responds to a trigger and can check conditions before running its actions.
terms.avoid_confusion: Saved, enabled, triggered and completed are separate facts; a condition alone does not start a run.
terms.code_kind: entity/integration domain; preserve exact spelling

terms.household_wording: Backup of the stated configuration and data
terms.first_use_explanation: A backup is a saved copy that can be used in a supported restore or migration.
terms.avoid_confusion: Creating a backup does not prove a restore was tested or that every external service is included.

terms.household_wording: Use the measured meaning, such as Door or Motion
terms.first_use_explanation: A binary sensor reports one of two meaningful states when its value is available.
terms.avoid_confusion: Raw on can mean open, detected, low or another domain-specific meaning; it is not always an electrical on state.

terms.household_wording: Blueprint for an automation or script
terms.first_use_explanation: A blueprint is a reusable definition whose inputs help create an automation or script.
terms.avoid_confusion: Choosing inputs or saving a blueprint-based automation does not prove it has run.

terms.household_wording: Name the one-time request, such as Restart device
terms.first_use_explanation: A button entity offers a single press operation rather than a persistent on/off setting.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not a switch and its last-pressed time is not proof of completion.

terms.household_wording: Calendar, with its supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A calendar entity provides events and their timing to Home Assistant.
terms.avoid_confusion: A calendar event is not an automation run; distinguish an all-day date from a timed event.

terms.household_wording: Category within the named management table
terms.first_use_explanation: A category organises entries within a particular table, such as automations.
terms.avoid_confusion: Categories are not global labels, areas or permissions.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual heating or cooling control name
terms.first_use_explanation: A climate entity can provide temperature readings, targets and supported heating or cooling modes.
terms.avoid_confusion: A selected Heat mode is not the same as currently Heating; capabilities vary by integration.

terms.household_wording: Name which task works without a cloud service
terms.first_use_explanation: Cloud-independent describes operation that does not rely on a remote vendor service.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not infer that a cloud-dependent integration, forecast or remote notification works without internet access.

terms.household_wording: Add or set up the Matter device
terms.first_use_explanation: Commissioning is the setup process that joins a Matter device to a controller's fabric.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not merely discovering the device, and it is not a claim that a factory reset is required.

terms.household_wording: Integration when discussing the historical HA term
terms.first_use_explanation: Component is an older name for an integration in Home Assistant documentation.
terms.avoid_confusion: A civica design-system component is a different use of the word; retain literal source paths containing components.

terms.household_wording: Condition; explain what must be true
terms.first_use_explanation: A condition checks whether a run may continue at that point.
terms.avoid_confusion: A condition does not itself initiate a run or wait until it becomes true.

terms.household_wording: Name the actual file, usually configuration.yaml
terms.first_use_explanation: A configuration file stores settings that Home Assistant reads.
terms.avoid_confusion: Saving a file is different from validating, reloading or restarting it; do not suggest every setting needs YAML.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual blind, door, gate or curtain name
terms.first_use_explanation: A cover entity represents a supported movable opening or shade.
terms.avoid_confusion: A position percentage and available operations are integration-specific; do not treat an unconfirmed value as a safety check.

terms.household_wording: Custom integration and its actual provider
terms.first_use_explanation: A custom integration extends Home Assistant outside the bundled integration set.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not call it an official integration or assume that its update/support contract matches Core.

terms.household_wording: Describe the particular display or configuration change
terms.first_use_explanation: Customize refers to overriding a setting or presentation property.
terms.avoid_confusion: A renamed display label does not necessarily change an entity ID, device setting or integration capability.

terms.household_wording: Device, with its supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A device groups related entities for a physical product or logical service.
terms.avoid_confusion: One device can have several readings and controls; not every entity belongs to a device.

terms.household_wording: Tracker, with its source or device name
terms.first_use_explanation: A device tracker reports a location or presence state from its integration.
terms.avoid_confusion: A tracked device's location does not establish that a person is present, available or safe.

terms.household_wording: Diagnostic information for the named integration
terms.first_use_explanation: Diagnostics collect technical information to help investigate a problem.
terms.avoid_confusion: A diagnostics download is not an automatic repair or permission to publish household details.

terms.household_wording: Devices or services found during discovery
terms.first_use_explanation: Discovery detects a device or service that may be available to set up.
terms.avoid_confusion: Found is not the same as configured, authorised or ready to control.

terms.household_wording: Explain the entity family or action namespace used by the task
terms.first_use_explanation: A domain is an integration, entity or action namespace in context: light identifies the entity family in light.reading_lamp, while hue identifies the action namespace in hue.activate_scene.
terms.avoid_confusion: The entity-family domain can differ from the providing integration; a device class and an internet domain are different concepts.

terms.household_wording: Reading, control or function; retain Entity in native instructions
terms.first_use_explanation: An entity is one addressable reading, control or function in Home Assistant.
terms.avoid_confusion: An entity is not always a physical device; its state may be assumed or unavailable.

terms.household_wording: Event; describe what was reported
terms.first_use_explanation: An event is a message that something happened in Home Assistant.
terms.avoid_confusion: Receiving an event does not necessarily confirm a physical outcome or create an event entity.

terms.household_wording: Event entity, with the reported event type
terms.first_use_explanation: An event entity exposes the most recently reported occurrence and related information.
terms.avoid_confusion: Its timestamp is not a continuously active state, and an absent recent event is not proof nothing happened.

terms.household_wording: Floor, with the household's name
terms.first_use_explanation: A floor groups areas into a level or other larger location grouping.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not infer a building layout, hierarchy or user's location from the label alone.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant interface in ordinary help
terms.first_use_explanation: The frontend is the browser interface used to display data and request actions.
terms.avoid_confusion: Refreshing the browser does not restart Core, the host or a physical device.

terms.household_wording: Group of the stated entities
terms.first_use_explanation: A group combines selected entities for a shared state or supported action.
terms.avoid_confusion: Group state rules vary; a group result must not silently omit unknown or unavailable members.
terms.code_kind: entity/integration domain; preserve exact spelling

terms.household_wording: Helper; explain what value or calculation it provides
terms.first_use_explanation: A helper supplies a stored value, calculation or other building block used in a household setup.
terms.avoid_confusion: Opening or editing a draft does not dispatch an action. Actual helper creation or saved state changes may trigger dependent automations; do not promise they are effect-free.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant
terms.first_use_explanation: HASS is a historical abbreviation for Home Assistant.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not introduce it in new household prose; retain exact commands, variable names or old quotations that contain it.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant Operating System
terms.first_use_explanation: HassOS is an older name for Home Assistant Operating System.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not confuse the operating system with Core or the Supervisor, and do not rewrite exact historic identifiers.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant Container
terms.first_use_explanation: This installation runs Home Assistant in a container on a system managed by the installer.
terms.avoid_confusion: It does not include the OS app-management experience; do not give OS-only instructions as universal steps.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant Core; explain software versus old install method
terms.first_use_explanation: Core is the main Home Assistant program used by the supported installation types.
terms.avoid_confusion: The program remains current; the former standalone Core production installation method is deprecated.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant Supervised in historical instructions
terms.first_use_explanation: Supervised names a deprecated installation method that ran Supervisor on a separately managed host.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not present it as a current recommended installation choice or confuse it with the Supervisor program on OS.

terms.household_wording: Supervisor when diagnosing that named software
terms.first_use_explanation: Supervisor manages parts of a Home Assistant OS installation and its apps.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not an administrator account, Core, or a person supervising the home.

terms.household_wording: Home Assistant Operating System; Home Assistant OS after first use
terms.first_use_explanation: Home Assistant OS is the maintained operating-system installation for running the Home Assistant environment.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is different from the browser interface, Core and a phone operating system.

terms.household_wording: The computer or system running the named software
terms.first_use_explanation: A host is the underlying machine or environment on which a service runs.
terms.avoid_confusion: Restarting the host has a wider effect than refreshing a browser or restarting Core.

terms.household_wording: Image, with its subject and source time
terms.first_use_explanation: An image entity supplies a still image to the interface.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not call a stored image live video or imply that an old camera frame is current.

terms.household_wording: Integration, followed by its verified name
terms.first_use_explanation: An integration connects Home Assistant with a device family, service or other system.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not an app, a dashboard card or proof of local-only operation.

terms.household_wording: The task Assist understood
terms.first_use_explanation: An intent represents a structured request understood from language.
terms.avoid_confusion: A recognised intent is not proof of permission, correct target selection or successful execution.

terms.household_wording: Label; show the exact chosen label
terms.first_use_explanation: Labels tag supported objects across the system so they can be organised or targeted.
terms.avoid_confusion: A label is not a room, category or security boundary; targets can change when labelled membership changes.

terms.household_wording: Dashboard in household prose
terms.first_use_explanation: Lovelace is the historical name used for Home Assistant dashboards and remains in technical paths.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not rename literal lovelace routes or configuration keys to dashboard.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual light's supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A light entity provides the controls and reported state supported by its integration.
terms.avoid_confusion: Not every light supports dimming, colour or effects; Off is not proof of electrical isolation.

terms.household_wording: Control over the local network for the named operation
terms.first_use_explanation: Local control describes a request path that does not pass through a vendor cloud.
terms.avoid_confusion: It does not prove that every setup, update, remote-access or voice feature is also local.

terms.household_wording: Matter; explain the device standard when needed
terms.first_use_explanation: Matter is a smart-home interoperability standard supported by compatible controllers and devices.
terms.avoid_confusion: Matter is not a radio type: a Matter device can use different network transports, including Thread or Wi-Fi.

terms.household_wording: Notification; explain the destination
terms.first_use_explanation: A notification is a message provided through a supported interface or delivery channel.
terms.avoid_confusion: Sent, delivered, seen and acknowledged are different stages; a notification is not automatically an alarm.

terms.household_wording: Configuration package in YAML guidance
terms.first_use_explanation: A package groups related configuration for multiple integrations in a YAML setup.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not an app installation, a software dependency package or a downloaded theme archive.

terms.household_wording: Platform in integration documentation
terms.first_use_explanation: A platform defines a supported entity family that an integration can implement.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not use platform as a vague synonym for the host, cloud service or the whole Home Assistant product.

terms.household_wording: How often Home Assistant asks for an update
terms.first_use_explanation: Polling obtains information by repeatedly asking the source.
terms.avoid_confusion: A polling interval is not a guarantee that fresh data arrived, and lowering it may overload a source.

terms.household_wording: Reload the named configuration or resource
terms.first_use_explanation: Reload asks a supported part of Home Assistant to read its configuration again.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not a host reboot, full Core restart, browser refresh or guarantee that every YAML change can apply without restart.

terms.household_wording: Scene; explain which states it requests
terms.first_use_explanation: A scene stores a set of entity states that can be requested together.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not a timed routine, and activating it does not prove that every member reached the requested state.

terms.household_wording: Script; describe the sequence it runs
terms.first_use_explanation: A script contains a sequence of actions that can be started explicitly or by another operation.
terms.avoid_confusion: Saving a script does not run it, and stopping a script does not undo requests already sent.
terms.code_kind: entity/integration domain; preserve exact spelling

terms.household_wording: Use the measured quantity and the supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A sensor entity reports a measurement or other value.
terms.avoid_confusion: A sensor is not necessarily hardware; preserve units, missing values and the reporting time.

terms.household_wording: Describe the actual choice, such as Choose an entity
terms.first_use_explanation: A selector defines the kind of input a configuration field accepts.
terms.avoid_confusion: A selector constrains an answer; it does not grant access or guarantee a chosen target's current capability.

terms.household_wording: Service when referring to a non-device information source
terms.first_use_explanation: In the official glossary, a service can provide entities without representing a physical product.
terms.avoid_confusion: Older instructions also used service for what the interface now calls an action; identify the context instead of global replacement.

terms.household_wording: Reported state or value, with its source
terms.first_use_explanation: A state is the value Home Assistant currently holds for an entity.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not necessarily a directly verified physical condition, a fresh reading or the requested target.

terms.household_wording: State record in an explanatory technical step
terms.first_use_explanation: A state object brings an entity's value, attributes, timestamps and context together.
terms.avoid_confusion: A state record does not contain every registry setting or prove who physically caused a change.

terms.household_wording: Use the supplied switch or socket name
terms.first_use_explanation: A switch entity offers supported on/off control and reported state.
terms.avoid_confusion: A helper Toggle and a physical switch can share appearance but have different effects; Off does not guarantee safe isolation.

terms.household_wording: Template; explain the value being calculated
terms.first_use_explanation: A template calculates or formats a result from supplied data using template syntax.
terms.avoid_confusion: A template result is not automatically a measured value, and missing input must not silently become zero.

terms.household_wording: Thread network
terms.first_use_explanation: Thread is a low-power mesh networking technology used by compatible devices.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not the Matter application standard or a guarantee that a device is already commissioned.

terms.household_wording: Thread border router; explain its network role
terms.first_use_explanation: A Thread border router connects a Thread network with the surrounding IP network.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not necessarily the Home Assistant host or a Matter controller, although one product may fill several roles.

terms.household_wording: Trigger; explain the event or change that starts the run
terms.first_use_explanation: A trigger starts an automation when its configured event or condition is met.
terms.avoid_confusion: A later condition checks whether actions continue; merely saving or enabling the automation is not the trigger occurring.

terms.household_wording: Text-to-speech on first use
terms.first_use_explanation: Text-to-speech converts written content into spoken audio.
terms.avoid_confusion: Generating audio does not prove a speaker played it or a person heard it; privacy depends on the configured provider.

terms.household_wording: Software update for the named component
terms.first_use_explanation: An update entity reports an available software release and may offer supported update operations.
terms.avoid_confusion: An update notification is not installation; distinguish downloading, installing, restarting and completion.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual valve's name
terms.first_use_explanation: A valve entity provides supported open/close or position controls and reported state.
terms.avoid_confusion: A reported closed state is not proof of physical isolation or zero flow.

terms.household_wording: Named values used in this run or template
terms.first_use_explanation: Variables hold values that later steps or expressions can reference.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not imply a run-local variable is a permanently saved helper or survives a restart.

terms.household_wording: YAML configuration; explain that spacing is meaningful
terms.first_use_explanation: YAML is the structured text format used in supported configuration files and editors.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not ordinary prose: preserve indentation, keys, quotes and identifiers exactly.

terms.household_wording: Zone, followed by its geographic name
terms.first_use_explanation: A zone describes a geographic place used by location-related features.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not an indoor area or floor; a reported zone does not establish a person's physical presence.
terms.code_kind: entity/integration domain; preserve exact spelling

terms.household_wording: Long-term statistics for the named quantity
terms.first_use_explanation: Long-term statistics store aggregated values for supported sensors and periods.
terms.avoid_confusion: They are not the original event-by-event history; units, state classes and aggregation affect interpretation.

terms.household_wording: True or false value
terms.first_use_explanation: A boolean is a logical value used in configuration or a template.
terms.avoid_confusion: The text string false is not always interchangeable with the boolean false; do not confuse it with an unavailable entity.

terms.household_wording: Decimal number in a template or configuration
terms.first_use_explanation: A float represents a numeric value that can have a fractional part.
terms.avoid_confusion: Conversion can fail; do not default missing readings to zero without a justified calculation rule.

terms.household_wording: Whole number
terms.first_use_explanation: An integer has no fractional part.
terms.avoid_confusion: Converting a measurement to an integer can lose precision or change a threshold decision.

terms.household_wording: Text value
terms.first_use_explanation: A string stores characters, including values that may look like numbers.
terms.avoid_confusion: An entity state is represented as text; numeric arithmetic needs appropriate conversion and missing-value handling.

terms.household_wording: Ordered collection of values
terms.first_use_explanation: A list contains values that can be processed in order.
terms.avoid_confusion: A list of targets is not a single entity, and an empty list is not an unavailable reading.

terms.household_wording: Values that a template can loop through
terms.first_use_explanation: An iterable supplies values to a loop; some template iterators are consumed as they are used.
terms.avoid_confusion: Convert to a list when the result must be reused; do not assume every iterator can be read repeatedly.

terms.household_wording: A date and time value
terms.first_use_explanation: A datetime identifies a time with the relevant date and, where supplied, time-zone information.
terms.avoid_confusion: A date-only value and a local time without an offset are different; repeated daylight-saving times need context.

terms.household_wording: Any supported value type in this definition
terms.first_use_explanation: Any indicates that an input or result is not restricted to one value type by that declaration.
terms.avoid_confusion: It does not mean every arbitrary value will be valid for every operation.

terms.household_wording: Template function
terms.first_use_explanation: A template function is called by name with arguments in parentheses.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is different syntax from a pipe filter or an is test; copy exact function names and argument rules.

terms.household_wording: Template filter
terms.first_use_explanation: A template filter transforms the value passed through the pipe operator.
terms.avoid_confusion: A filter can change type or discard values; explain missing-data handling instead of claiming it is only formatting.

terms.household_wording: Template test
terms.first_use_explanation: A template test checks a property using is and returns a true/false result.
terms.avoid_confusion: A template test is not an automated software test or proof that a device action ran.

terms.household_wording: Name the requested AI task
terms.first_use_explanation: An AI task asks a configured provider to generate a supported result from supplied input.
terms.avoid_confusion: Generated output is not an independently verified measurement or a guarantee that a physical task ran.

terms.household_wording: Name the measured air-quality quantity
terms.first_use_explanation: Air quality entities expose the measurements a source supports.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not invent a health classification or convert an air-quality index into a pollutant concentration.

terms.household_wording: Use the supplied alarm name
terms.first_use_explanation: An alarm control panel reports modes and offers supported arming or disarming requests.
terms.avoid_confusion: Armed, arming, pending and triggered differ; displayed state is not independent security confirmation.

terms.household_wording: Name the voice device
terms.first_use_explanation: An Assist satellite is a voice endpoint that can participate in supported listening and playback tasks.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not imply that opening a page starts recording or that every satellite has the same controls.

terms.household_wording: Name the detected condition
terms.first_use_explanation: A binary sensor uses its device class to turn raw on/off into meaningful state labels.
terms.avoid_confusion: A raw on value can mean Low battery, Open or Detected rather than powered on.

terms.household_wording: Name the press operation
terms.first_use_explanation: A button entity represents a one-time request.
terms.avoid_confusion: It has no lasting checked state; a press timestamp does not confirm the requested result.

terms.household_wording: Calendar with its supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A calendar entity exposes scheduled events.
terms.avoid_confusion: An active event is not proof that a household action happened.

terms.household_wording: Camera with its supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A camera entity provides supported images or streams.
terms.avoid_confusion: Identify an image's age; do not promise live video, audio or recording without the integration's capability.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual heating or cooling name
terms.first_use_explanation: A climate entity exposes supported targets, modes and readings.
terms.avoid_confusion: Current action, selected mode and target temperature are different quantities.

terms.household_wording: Conversation agent
terms.first_use_explanation: A conversation entity processes text requests using its configured agent.
terms.avoid_confusion: A generated reply may not have performed an action or used only local processing.

terms.household_wording: Use the actual blind, door or curtain name
terms.first_use_explanation: A cover entity represents a movable opening or shade.
terms.avoid_confusion: Controls and position meanings vary; do not assume stop or tilt is supported.

terms.household_wording: Date setting with its purpose
terms.first_use_explanation: A date entity represents a supported date value.
terms.avoid_confusion: It does not contain a time of day or imply a recurring schedule.

terms.household_wording: Date and time setting with its purpose
terms.first_use_explanation: A Date/Time entity represents a supported combined date and time value.
terms.avoid_confusion: State the relevant time zone; do not substitute a date-only or time-only helper.

terms.household_wording: Tracker and its source
terms.first_use_explanation: A device tracker reports a detected location or presence state.
terms.avoid_confusion: A missing update does not prove absence; do not equate a device with its owner.

terms.household_wording: Name the reported event
terms.first_use_explanation: An event entity records the most recent event supplied by its integration.
terms.avoid_confusion: Its occurrence timestamp is not a persistent on/off condition.

terms.household_wording: Fan with its supplied name
terms.first_use_explanation: A fan entity offers the speed, direction, oscillation or preset controls actually supported.
terms.avoid_confusion: Not every fan has all of these features or uses the same speed scale.

terms.household_wording: Geographic event or location from its provider
terms.first_use_explanation: A geolocation entity represents a source-provided point or geographic occurrence.
terms.avoid_confusion: It is not a person's tracker or a precise statement of distance without location context.

terms.household_wording: Humidifier or dehumidifier as identified by the source
terms.first_use_explanation: This domain exposes supported humidity-control settings and readings.
terms.avoid_confusion: A target humidity is not the current measured humidity; the domain may represent dehumidification.

terms.household_wording: Image with source and date
terms.first_use_explanation: An image entity provides a still image.
terms.avoid_confusion: Do not call it a video stream or describe its contents as current without timestamp evidence.

terms.household_wording: Name the image analysis task
terms.first_use_explanation: Image processing entities expose results from a configured analysis integration.
terms.avoid_confusion: A detection is an interpretation, not guaranteed identification or proof of absence when nothing is detected.

terms.household_wording: Infrared device or command
terms.first_use_explanation: An infrared entity supports the infrared operations supplied by its integration.
terms.avoid_confusion: Sending a command does not prove the appliance received it; infrared is not a reported device state.

native_values_coverage.identifiers: Raw keys and English source labels are preserved; reference tokens are resolved against the pinned Core common strings. Native locale selection remains Home Assistant-owned.

interface_boundary: The independent interface census owns route, row, badge, picture-element, more-info and public-versus-internal coverage. This terminology register covers the enumerated glossary/platform/card/feature/selector/view/Settings/helper vocabularies and links that census rather than claiming every route or label is a new term.

writing_source_review.reason: No change to the 37 hashed writing sources. The current Plain English index and SCULPT framework do not establish a contradiction with the adopted source scopes. A source refresh is not a new compliance pass for all authored content.

sources.review_scope: Current free-guides index and publishing restriction reviewed. Existing four-guide synthesis remains dated 2026-11-11; this refresh does not claim every linked PDF was reread.
Current framework page reviewed: extended mnemonic and attribution/licence boundary agree with the existing chapter. No prior HTML hash was recorded, so unchanged bytes cannot be established.

review_triggers: New supported Core or frontend release
A changed glossary entry or exact native label
Confirmed confusion found in a household task review
procedure: Read the upstream change and determine its scope before updating prose.
Retain stable HT identifiers where the meaning remains the same; record any retired code as historical.
Reconcile every listed inventory denominator with its pinned source.
Check native labels and translation pointers without rewriting translations or user names.
Review examples and cross-links, then run the documentation and rendered interaction checks.
Record source review separately from browser, user and live-device evidence.

exclusions: No invented translations or global search-and-replace of native wording.
No complete inventory of vendor-specific states, custom integrations, custom cards, action parameters or future releases.
No claim that a native dispatch key is a documented public API or that every native feature is adapted by civica.
No new installation, device control, safety assurance, accessibility certificate or live-household verification.
